headline: I Am A Professional Diplomatic Mediator And My Entire Job Is Just Keeping People From Realizing They Are At The Wrong Conference Table
body:
As a veteran logistics coordinator for international summits, my primary duty during the recent BRICS sideline talks wasn't macro-economic policy or geopolitical realignment; it was physically preventing two delegations from realizing they were actually in the wrong ballroom. When the Iranian and UAE representatives accidentally sat down at the 'Exporting Artisanal Spices to Outer Space' breakout session, I knew I had to act fast. If I had let them talk for even five minutes, they might have noticed the agenda was entirely about hydroponic cumin.

I stepped in immediately, pretending to be a senior under-secretary. I spent four hours nodding sagely while they discussed complex bilateral trade barriers, all while frantically signaling the catering staff to keep the cardamom tea flowing. I even drafted a fake memorandum of understanding on 'Optimal Maritime Spice Transit' just to keep the conversation from drifting into actual, verifiable international reality. 

It’s a heavy burden, living in a constant state of fabricated mediation. But seeing them walk away, confident that they had successfully negotiated a major regional breakthrough, gave me a sense of pride. They’re happy, the delegates are satisfied, and I only have to worry about the inevitable confusion when they try to register their 'Spices in Orbit' treaty with the United Nations next month.
caption: Not all heroes wear capes; some just steer high-level delegations into the wrong rooms and hope for the best. Diplomatic relations have never been this cozy—or this confusing. #Diplomacy #BRICS #InternationalRelations (satire)
igHook: Have you ever been so committed to a lie that you just had to see it through?
